disagreements: Depth: my plain random-phase box depth (median baseline, unmasked 1 d running median) is 1490 +- 59 ppm vs pipeline pass-2 1569 +- 62 ppm (1.1 sigma). Addendum shows this is an estimator effect: my unmasked running median includes the ~2.4 in-transit cadences, depressing the trend by ~60 ppm around each transit (a +50-100 ppm hump at phases +-0.1-0.2 in the 20-bin phase curve). The FLUX_ERR-weighted depth on the same detrended data is 1567 ppm and astropy compute_stats gives 1568 +- 55 ppm, matching the pipeline. The pipeline's masked re-detrend value is the better estimator; mine is biased low by ~4 %.

Secondary at phase 0.5: I measure -189 +- 58 ppm (-3.2 sigma, i.e. a BRIGHTENING) vs pipeline -222 ppm at -4.0 sigma. Same sign and comparable size, but my significance is lower, and relative to the mean (not median) out-of-transit level it is only ~-130 ppm (~2.3 sigma). It is confined to ~1 h at phase 0.50 (scan 0.40-0.60: extreme exactly at 0.50; adjacent box at 0.48 is +89 ppm), present in all four years at 0.5-2.5 sigma each, and there is no broad reflection/ellipsoidal phase curve (cos/sin harmonics all < 40 ppm). I read it as a marginal 2-3 sigma feature rather than a 4 sigma one; no secondary ECLIPSE is seen (a dip deeper than ~120 ppm at phase 0.5 is excluded at 2 sigma).

Depth stability: the pipeline's per-time-quartile depths (1957, 1601, 1091, 1566 ppm, each +-~110) imply chi2 ~ 32 for 3 dof by my arithmetic, whereas my per-Kepler-year box depths (1713 +- 137, 1500 +- 123, 1323 +- 121, 1454 +- 107) give chi2 = 4.7/3 and per-quarter depths give chi2 = 20.4/16, with no roll-season dependence (chi2 = 3.8/3). Both agree the third time-chunk is shallowest, but the pipeline's per-event local-depth estimator shows considerably more scatter than my global-box estimator. Not resolved here; worth a look at events.csv before anything is claimed about depth constancy.

Odd/even labels are swapped between the two analyses (my t0 is 307 = odd cycles after the pipeline's), so my odd (1560) corresponds to their even (1632) and my even (1421) to their odd (1507); the difference is 1.14 sigma in both, so no real disagreement.

Duration/shape: box duration agrees (1.15 h vs 1.125 h, same grid step), but my unconstrained trapezoid fit is degenerate (depth 2165 +- 1405 ppm, T14 1.71 +- 0.08 h, T23/T14 ~ 0, i.e. V-shaped). With only ~2.35 long-cadence samples per transit the ingress/egress shape is unresolved; the pipeline's core_to_box ratio 1.20 and my V-shaped fit are both consistent with cadence smearing of a short (~1 h), likely high-impact-parameter (b ~ 0.8 for Rstar 0.70) event and should not be read as a shape measurement.

SDE: my 'SDE' is (max - mean)/std of the astropy likelihood periodogram over my own 1-50 d grid (108.1 raw, 117.8 after flattening the periodogram; inverted-flux null on the same grid 7.5 / 9.6). This is not the same statistic as the pipeline's BLS SDE or the TLS SDE of 22.2 and should not be compared numerically; the point is that the peak is overwhelmingly the strongest and the inverted null is flat.

# Independent re-derivation: kic-009520080 (KIC 9520080, Gaia DR3 2127366472162960768)

Date 2026-10-17. Own code only (numpy/scipy/astropy; no `pipeline/` imports, no wotan, no TLS). All numbers below are in `/home/user/ZyushgPlanet/runs/poolA_main/adversarial/kic-009520080/rederive/rederive_results.json` (main run) and `rederive_addendum.json` (follow-ups); figure `rederive_fold.png`; logs `rederive_run.log`, `rederive_addendum.log`. Target: G = 17.49, BP-RP 1.25, Teff 4546 K, Rstar 0.70 Rsun, d = 1657 pc, RUWE 1.15; KBONUS psffrac 0.614, crowdsap 0.983, flfrcsap 0.858, 2-pixel SAP aperture; originating TPF KIC 9520088.

## 1. Loading and detrending
`LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED`, `SAP_QUALITY == 0`, finite, FLUX > 0: 57 624 cadences, baseline 1459.5 d (Q1-Q17). Per-quarter median normalisation; iterative 1.0 d time-based running median (3 iterations, points > 3 sigma from the trend excluded from the trend estimate); final clip at +4 / -15 sigma leaves 57 493 points. Robust point scatter 1893 ppm (median FLUX_ERR 1818 ppm, so the formal errors are realistic).

## 2. Blind BLS 1-50 d (own grid)
Log-uniform grid, 475 798 periods (oversample 2.5 relative to dmin/baseline), 8 durations 0.03-0.22 d, astropy `BoxLeastSquares` likelihood objective. Top three mutually distinct peaks: **2.37702 d (power 398.7)**, 4.75399 d (210.2, = 2P), 1.18851 d (169.9, = P/2). The pipeline period 2.37700 d is the top peak, not an alias. SDE (max-mean)/std = 108.1 raw, 117.8 after median-flattening the periodogram. Inverted-flux null (2 - f) on the identical grid: best 24.20 d, SDE 7.5 / 9.6. **recovered_blind = true.**

## 3. Measurements at the refined ephemeris (PSF FLUX)
Refined P = 2.3770140 d, t0 = BKJD 861.89886 (BJD 2455694.89886, placed mid-baseline), box duration 0.048 d = 1.15 h (grid step 0.06 h).
- Primary box depth (plain mean in box vs median out-of-box; error = std of 3000 random-phase boxes): **1490 +- 59 ppm, empirical SNR 25.4**. Same data, FLUX_ERR-weighted: 1567 ppm; astropy `compute_stats`: 1568 +- 55 ppm. The spread is explained in the addendum: my unmasked running median absorbs ~60 ppm of the transit (hump of +50-100 ppm at phases +-0.1-0.2), so 1490 is biased low by ~4 %; 1550-1570 ppm is the better value.
- Odd 1560 +- 95 ppm, even 1421 +- 77 ppm: **1.14 sigma**.
- Phase 0.5 box: **-189 +- 58 ppm (-3.2 sigma)** = a brightening, not an eclipse. Per year: -137 +- 134, -275 +- 120, -298 +- 120, -57 +- 107 ppm. Narrow (~1 h, extreme exactly at phase 0.50; adjacent 0.48 box is +89 ppm); relative to the mean rather than the median baseline it is ~-130 ppm (2.3 sigma). Harmonic fit of the out-of-transit phase curve: cos1 +38 +- 12, sin1 +8 +- 12, cos2 +15 +- 12, sin2 -9 +- 12 ppm, i.e. no reflection or ellipsoidal modulation above ~40 ppm. No secondary eclipse: a dip >= ~120 ppm at phase 0.5 is excluded at 2 sigma.
- Per-year depths: 1713 +- 137, 1500 +- 123, 1323 +- 121, 1454 +- 107 ppm (chi2 4.7 / 3 dof). Per-quarter (17 values, random-phase errors): chi2 20.4 / 16; lowest Q10 866 +- 269, Q15 1089 +- 183. Per Kepler roll season: 1686 +- 122, 1379 +- 136, 1423 +- 88, 1476 +- 138 (chi2 3.8 / 3): no season-dependent contamination signature.
- Transits: 614 windows in the baseline, **542 epochs with at least one quality-0 cadence in the box**, 476 with >= half the expected 2.35 cadences; 1175 in-transit cadences in total.
- Shape: trapezoid least squares is degenerate (depth 2165 +- 1405 ppm, T14 1.71 h, T23/T14 ~ 0). With ~2.35 long-cadence samples per event the shape is unresolved. For Rstar 0.70 / M ~ 0.7 Msun the maximal central duration is ~2.0 h, so 1.15 h implies b ~ 0.8 if on target; (depth)^0.5 x 0.70 Rsun gives ~3.0 Re for 1490-1570 ppm.

## 4. SAP_FLUX dilution check
Same pipeline on SAP_FLUX (57 477 points, scatter 1943 ppm): primary **1396 +- 56 ppm** (SNR 25.1), phase-0.5 box -186 +- 56 ppm, free BLS near the peak recovers P = 2.377018 d, 1.15 h, 1484 +- 50 ppm. **SAP/PSF depth ratio 0.94 +- 0.05.** With crowdsap 0.983 the expected ratio for an on-target signal is ~0.98; 0.94 is consistent (0.8 sigma) and the SAP aperture does not show a deeper signal than the PSF flux, as it would if a brighter neighbour inside the aperture were the source. This is a weak test: both products come from the same 2-4 pixels, so it cannot discriminate a source within ~1 pixel of the target, and it says nothing about the G = 14.8 star at ~10'' or the G = 13.9 star at ~19'' except that they would have to leak a ~1500 ppm/(contamination fraction) eclipse into a nearly clean aperture. That is the pixel-level test's job, not this one's.

## 5. Comparison with the pipeline (vet.json read only after the above)
Period 2.3770140 vs 2.3770144 d (3e-7 d, 0.3 min over the baseline); t0 differs by exactly 307 cycles with a 1.3 min residual; duration 1.15 vs 1.125 h; depth 1490 +- 59 (plain box) / 1567 (weighted) vs 1569 +- 62; empirical SNR 25.4 vs 28.3; odd/even 1.14 vs 1.13 sigma (labels swapped by the odd cycle offset); secondary -189 (-3.2 sigma) vs -222 (-4.0 sigma); transits 542 / 476 vs n_events 468 and TLS distinct 540; Rp ~3.0 Re vs 3.03 Re. **The signal, period, epoch, depth, duration, odd/even and the sign of the phase-0.5 feature all reproduce with independent code.** Honest disagreements are in the list: (i) my unmasked detrend under-measures depth by ~4 %, so the pipeline's masked value is preferred; (ii) I find the phase-0.5 brightening at 2-3 sigma rather than 4 sigma, and it is narrow with no accompanying phase curve; (iii) the pipeline's per-quartile depths scatter far more (chi2 ~32/3) than my per-year/per-quarter/per-season depths (4.7/3, 20.4/16, 3.8/3), which should be looked at in events.csv; (iv) transit shape is unconstrained at long cadence and should not be used as evidence either way.

## What this does and does not establish
A 2.377 d, ~1.1 h, ~1500 ppm periodic box-shaped dimming is present in the KBONUS PSF and SAP light curves of KIC 9520080 with no odd/even difference, no secondary eclipse, constant depth across years and roll seasons, and a clean inverted null. It is a first-screen/stage-2 **signal**; nothing here localises it on the sky, and the SAP/PSF ratio cannot exclude a blend within a pixel. The 2-3 sigma brightening at phase 0.5 is unexplained and should be carried forward as an open item rather than dismissed or over-read.
sap_vs_psf_depth: SAP_FLUX box depth 1396 +- 56 ppm vs PSF FLUX 1490 +- 59 ppm at the same ephemeris (free BLS on SAP near the peak: 1484 +- 50 ppm, P 2.377018 d, 1.15 h); ratio SAP/PSF = 0.94 +- 0.05. KBONUS crowdsap for the 2-pixel aperture is 0.983, so an on-target signal predicts a ratio ~0.98; the measured 0.94 is consistent with that (0.8 sigma) and SAP is not deeper than PSF, so there is no sign that the aperture sees a brighter contaminating eclipse. Weak test: both products derive from the same few pixels, so it cannot exclude a blend within ~1 pixel and does not address the G=14.8 (~10 arcsec) or G=13.9 (~19 arcsec) neighbours; pixel-level localisation is required for that.
